topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the class and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: PAMPs, DAMPs, and self versus non-self discrimination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system identifies infections and tissue damage by recognizing conserved molecular patterns that distinguish self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and intracellular signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genetics, cellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptors that transduce danger signals into inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Initiation of inflammation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell extravasation into tissues, drain antigens to lymph nodes, and can trigger severe systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic persistence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms required to terminate inflammatory signaling, orchestrate tissue healing, and manage uncleared pathogens through chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on complement.
